page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture at 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, along with hardware cryptography support via AES and SHA extensions. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local ephemeral storage is bundled with the instance, requiring reliance on remote persistent storage, and no GPU hardware accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate balanced compute performance and responsive memory access. In standard CPU benchmarks, the platform produced average-tier results with 1,949.59 in stress-ng single-core and 15,802.38 in multi-core metrics, matched by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,292.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 26,412.49. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 123.05 GB/s, while write bandwidth measured 68.96 GB/s. The instance demonstrated strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 31.4 GB/s. Additionally, integrated AMX execution units enabled elevated text generation speeds of 366.52 tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models, scoring in the top ten percent for that benchmark class.

The hardware configuration provides high memory density per compute core, making it cost efficient for memory-bound applications without paying for unneeded accelerator silicon. An operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, which places all I/O requirements on attached network storage disks. The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high L3 cache allocation make the E16s_v6 well suited for running memory-intensive workloads including Redis caching tiers, relational database engines, analytics processing, and CPU-driven small model machine learning inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure E16s_v6 is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz, paired with a 260 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. System capacity includes 128.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating remote persistent storage for all persistent data. Benchmark evaluations reveal solid mid-tier performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and elevated small-model LLM generation throughput. This hardware profile makes the E16s_v6 suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise analytics, and lightweight CPU-driven inference pipelines.
